why: Count the density: over 100 real data points in one 652px window (14 BOM lines with status, supplier and lead, 14 Gantt bars on a dated axis, 7 PO fields, 5 feed events), with hierarchy carried by 13px type and one green bar among grey ones, and the before and after states driven by a single data attribute plus CSS offsets.

Every row shows name, supplier, draggable bar, spare line and computed date, and all of it derives from one plan() function, so the dark critical row, the build line, the spare counts, the +21d or -15d tag and the Reset link are states of real logic and not drawn mockups.

Notice the transparent textarea stacked on a highlighted pre, the rank-based graph where only the critical path gets the heavy green stroke, and that an error is a designed state: the last good plan stays up, the bad line is tinted and the message names the line number.

Specifics carry this section: 6 PO numbers, 5 named suppliers, exact dates, amber only where a date moved, three text levels on dark and one unfinished line that keeps the log alive, while the six supplier marks differ in weight, tracking, case and glyph and are not grey clones.

Notice what replaces the tier grid: five lines with one opening, bold sans against serif, so the list reads as a rule; one sentence that defines the only paid unit; and a CTA that opens a real form with local CSV parsing, an inline error and a confirmation that quotes what it read.
